text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to $150.80, driven by a sharp spike in global oil prices amid escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude hit $116 a barrel—a six-month high—after Saudi Arabia reported intercepting Iranian-backed Houthi missiles and drones, and as the Trump administration signaled it may take action against Iran. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost the value of reserves and cash flow from production.

The stock's broader 12.45% gain over two weeks reflects a sustained rally as geopolitical risk in the Middle East has tightened global oil supplies. U.S. oil is trading at $107.89 a barrel versus the world price of $115.22, showing investors are pricing in real supply concerns—exactly the kind of environment that benefits large integrated oil producers with global operations.
